1. REQUESTED SERVICE & ACTION TAKEN


Healthfirst has reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider on October 22, 2026. Based on
clinical review against established Medical Necessity Criteria, coverage for the following service has been DENIED:


 Requested Service / Procedure                       Diagnosis / Codes          Setting Requested      Determination

 Elective Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA), Left        Primary Osteoarthritis,    Inpatient Acute        DENIED
 Knee                                                Left Knee                  Hospital Stay          (Inpatient Setting Not
 CPT 27447 - Arthroplasty, knee, condyle and         ICD-10 M17.12              2-Day Planned          Medically Necessary)
 plateau; medial and lateral compartments                                       Admission


2. CLINICAL RATIONALE & CLINICAL CRITERIA APPLIED



   Reason for Adverse Determination:

   Your physician requested approval for a planned inpatient acute care hospital admission following an elective
   left total knee replacement. While the surgical procedure itself (CPT 27447) is a covered benefit under your
   Healthfirst Silver Leaf Plan, our Medical Utilization Management Committee has determined that an acute care
   inpatient admission and hospital stay is NOT medically necessary for your clinical profile.

   Clinical Review Guidelines Used: MCG™ Health Care Guidelines (28th Edition) – Inpatient & Surgical Care:
   Arthroplasty, Knee, Total (S-700) & Healthfirst Clinical Policy #MM-041 (Surgical Care Setting Determination).

   Detailed Rationale: Medical records provided by Dr. Marcus Thorne (dated 10/10/2026 and 10/18/2026) show
   that you are 52 years old with primary knee osteoarthritis. Clinical review indicates that you do not possess
   active high-risk co-morbid conditions (such as severe uncontrolled congestive heart failure, severe COPD
   requiring active oxygen adjustment, or end-stage renal disease) that necessitate acute overnight inpatient
   telemetry or intensive acute nursing care. Current evidence-based clinical guidelines mandate that elective total
   knee replacements in functional adults without severe unstable systemic disease be performed in an outpatient
   surgical setting or under observation status (under 24 hours). Therefore, inpatient admission is denied.

3. HOW TO APPEAL THIS DECISION (YOUR APPEAL RIGHTS)


If you or your doctor disagree with this decision, you have the right to request an Internal Appeal. Requesting an
appeal means asking Healthfirst medical doctors to re-review your case along with any additional medical evidence
provided.



   Important Deadline: You must submit your appeal within 180 calendar days from the date of this notice (April 25,
   2027). There is no cost to file an appeal. You may represent yourself, or choose an authorized representative (such as
   your physician) to act on your behalf.



4. INTERNAL APPEAL OPTIONS & PROCEDURES


Standard Internal Appeal:


A decision will be made in writing within 30 calendar days of receiving your appeal request. You or your physician
should submit additional clinical documentation, such as functional status notes, home support limitations, or
medical risk factors not previously provided.


Expedited (Fast-Track) Appeal:


If your doctor certifies that waiting 30 days for a standard appeal could seriously jeopardize your life, health, or ability
to regain maximum function, you may request an Expedited Appeal. Expedited decisions are delivered verbally and in
writing within 72 hours.


5. WHERE AND HOW TO FILE YOUR APPEAL


You can file your appeal by mail, phone, fax, or online using the contact details below:


 By Mail:                          Healthfirst Appeals & Grievances Department
                                   P.O. Box 5166, New York, NY 10274-5166

 By Phone:                         1-888-250-2220 (TTY/TDD: 1-888-211-1777)
                                   Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM EST

 By Fax:                           1-646-313-4615 (Attention: Clinical Appeals Unit)

 Online Portal:                    Log in to your member account at my.healthfirst.org


6. NEW YORK STATE EXTERNAL APPEAL RIGHTS


Under New York Insurance Law, if Healthfirst upholds this denial upon internal appeal (or if Healthfirst waives the
internal appeal requirement), you have the right to file an External Appeal with the New York State Department of
Financial Services (DFS). An independent medical panel will review the denial. You must file for a NY State External
Appeal within 4 months of receiving Healthfirst's final adverse determination.
